name: RFC → Implementation
intent: Build what was decided, with evidence, without widening the change.

steps.name: Assemble the context and map the subsystem
steps.note: This is the READ and MAP of the working loop, done once for the whole workflow.

steps.name: Decompose into a dependency-ordered task graph
State the contracts before touching them
steps.applies_when: the change touches an API operation, channel topic, public function or resource attribute

steps.name: Tests that fail before and pass after
Independent review of the diff
steps.note: `security.dependencies` is here because WF-015 Release carried it alone, and a workflow that alone carries a capability is the only candidate for every work item that needs it — so every dependency-shaped task routed to the release lane at T4 behind the `protected` gate, whatever it actually was. An independent review of an earlier change found it by testing the diagnosis that had been written down instead (that the bare keyword `ship` was to blame, which was wrong: removing `ship` cost three real release routes, one of them to the Incident workflow, and left the misroute in place). Adding a dependency is ordinary implementation work and deserves a dependency-security review here; measured after, a dependency title has three candidate workflows instead of one and lands on WF-002.

steps.name: Moduledocs, spec updates and the documentation the change made false

escalations.when: implementation requires a contract change the RFC did not anticipate
the same step fails three times
a boundary in a design decision would have to move

completion: the lane's gates are green or reported unavailable with what that leaves unverified
a test distinguishes the change from its absence
the diff contains nothing the task did not require
review findings are resolved or recorded
memory: what the obvious implementation got wrong
any contract that turned out to be undocumented
evaluation: gate pass rate on first attempt
